query: Nexus-Entry-Z events affecting cash-withdrawal counts from 1996-11-13 through 1997-01-07, especially maintenance recurrence and security-driven foot traffic

evidence.claim: Security personnel are scheduled to leave the Annex throughout the forecast horizon, and management expects surrounding foot traffic to change.
evidence.exact_quote:
Per the updated Security Master Schedule, security staff are scheduled to be redirected from the Annex to the main terminal starting on 1996-11-13. This redirection of resources will conclude on 1997-01-07. 

Management anticipates that this scheduled shift in security personnel will result in a change to foot traffic patterns around the machine. Without the constant presence of stationed guards, pedestrian flow is expected to revert to previous unregulated patterns.

evidence.claim: Retrospective monitoring covering the complete forecast horizon found no recurrence of prior maintenance interruptions and 99.9% network uptime.
evidence.exact_quote: A summary of the observation period from 1996-05-29 to 1997-01-07 confirms no recurrence of 1995 service interruptions. Throughout these 223 days of monitoring, the Nexus-Entry-Z unit maintained 99.9% network uptime, with no recorded instances of the hardware failures or connectivity drops that necessitated the previous winter's decommissioning.

impacts.rationale: The security reassignment exactly spans the forecast horizon and is expected to alter nearby foot traffic, but the document gives neither the direction nor magnitude of any effect on withdrawal counts.

The full-horizon retrospective confirms that the earlier interruption regime did not recur and that network availability stayed near continuous, supporting preservation of the normal operating level rather than imposing forecast-period outage zeros.

missing_information: The corpus does not quantify how the security reassignment and resulting foot-traffic change affected the number of cash withdrawals, so no directional or numerical adjustment can be justified.
